column11: source

CMS Medicare Part B 2024 (drug_demand, asset 7308, brand 'Rybrevant'): $70,056,728.40 over 839 beneficiaries = $83,500.27 a beneficiary a year. Part B is the channel for this product: 839 beneficiaries against 28 in Part D in the same year. The figure is amivantamab's alone, billed under HCPCS J9061, 'injection, amivantamab-vmjw, 2 mg'; the realised allowed amount in the demand file is $19.92 a unit against a Medicare payment limit for J9061 of $19.975 to $20.673 across the four quarters of 2024, which is the check that the 2 mg unit is the right one
column12: the asset line is a combined brand and this price is the Rybrevant component only; Lazcluze is an oral tablet under Part D and carries a price of its own that is not in this row. Both colorectal studies and the head and neck study below give amivantamab without lazertinib, so amivantamab's own per-beneficiary figure is the right basis for the layers this file prices. Scale: at the same unit price a full labelled year of 1,050 mg (four weekly doses then every two weeks, 28 infusions in 52 weeks) is $292,862, and a 2024 beneficiary consumed 0.285 of it

column11: Social Security Act section 1847A: Medicare Part B pays 106% of the average sales price, and ASP is already net of manufacturer discounts and rebates, so the only deduction from the CMS allowed amount is the statutory 6% add-on, 1 - 1/1.06 = 0.056604. This is the deduction the book applies to every Part B anchor (backend/gross_to_net.py), the same one the Opdivo and ABP 206 seeds take
column12: direction checked: 0.0566 off list leaves $78,774 a beneficiary a year. Medicaid rebates and 340B discounts sit outside ASP and are not deducted here, which is the case for a larger deduction. Deducting a WAC-to-ASP gap on top of a Part B allowed amount would count the discount twice

column11: CMS Part B 2024 (drug_demand, asset 7308): 3,516,444 dosage units over 839 beneficiaries = 4,191 units a beneficiary, and J9061 is one unit per 2 mg, so 8,382 mg. A full labelled year is 29,400 mg: 1,050 mg for a patient under 80 kg, weekly for the first four weeks and then every two weeks, 28 infusions in 52 weeks (RYBREVANT USPI). 8,382 / 29,400 = 0.2851, so 1 - 0.2851 = 0.7149. The ratio is steady across the series: 0.327 (2022), 0.305 (2023), 0.285 (2024)
column12: the least certain number on this asset. It is measured on Medicare beneficiaries in 2022 to 2024, which is overwhelmingly the post-platinum EGFR exon 20 insertion population amivantamab was first approved in, where time on drug is short. The first-line regimen the product now sells into is far more durable: MARIPOSA reported median progression-free survival of 23.7 months against 16.6 on osimertinib, hazard ratio 0.70 (Cho BC et al., N Engl J Med 2024;391(16):1486-1498, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2403614, PMID 38924756), and at a constant hazard 1 - exp(-ln2/1.975) = 0.296, less than half this figure. It is stated at the measured value because the house identity needs the discontinuation rate and the per-beneficiary price measured on the same patients, and because a patient at 1,400 mg consumes more mg a year than the 1,050 mg denominator assumes, which biases the measured ratio down. A reader who thinks the layers below will be dosed and tolerated like MARIPOSA should roughly halve it, and should move the price with it

Colorectal Neoplasms
column11: two shares multiplied. 23% of US colorectal cancers are distant at diagnosis, against 34% localized, 37% regional and 6% unstaged (SEER Cancer Stat Facts, colorectal cancer, stage distribution 2016 to 2022). Of metastatic colorectal cancers, 33% are RAS and BRAF wild-type, which is exactly the population both Phase 3 studies enrol: in 2,118 molecularly classified patients from three Nordic population-based and real-world cohorts, KRAS mutations were seen in 49%, NRAS in 4%, BRAF-V600E in 14% and RAS and BRAF wild-type in 33% (Osterlund E, Ristimaki A, Nunes L et al., 'KRAS and NRAS mutations in Nordic population-based and real-world metastatic colorectal cancer cohorts', BJC Reports 2025;3, doi:10.1038/s44276-025-00188-5, PMID 41120702). 0.23 x 0.33 = 0.0759, about 12,057 patients a year
column12: a floor rather than a central estimate, and the omission that makes it one is relapse: it counts only disease that is distant at diagnosis and leaves out the stage II and stage III patients who relapse into metastatic disease, who are a large further inflow and are explicitly eligible for NCT06750094, which enrols recurrent as well as unresectable and metastatic disease. Pushing the other way, NCT06662786 is restricted to left-sided tumours and no sidedness filter is applied here, and neither study's performance-status and prior-therapy filters are applied

Colorectal Neoplasms
column11: a judgement. Both Phase 3 studies run head to head against the standard of care in this exact population: NCT06662786 against cetuximab with mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI in first line, NCT06750094 against cetuximab or bevacizumab with FOLFIRI after one prior line. Amivantamab would displace cetuximab rather than add to it, so the realistic ceiling is the share of RAS and BRAF wild-type patients who actually receive an EGFR-directed agent, not the whole eligible pool
column12: the case for lower, and it is a strong one: among 1,607 US patients with left-sided RAS/RAF wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer on first-line chemotherapy, only 186, 12%, received an anti-EGFR agent, rising from 9% in 2013 to 16% in 2018 (Nevala-Plagemann C, Iyengar S, Trunk AD, Pappas L, Haaland B, Garrido-Laguna I, J Natl Compr Canc Netw 2022;20(3):268-275, doi:10.6004/jnccn.2021.7079, PMID 35120306). The case for higher: a bispecific that beats cetuximab on progression-free survival would change that share, which is what both studies are designed to show, and it would also take second-line patients cetuximab never reached. Settled by years of sales, not by an event

column11: two shares multiplied. More than 90% of head and neck cancers are squamous cell carcinomas (Vigneswaran N, Williams MD, 'Epidemiologic trends in head and neck cancer and aids in diagnosis', Oral Maxillofac Surg Clin North Am 2014;26(2):123-141, doi:10.1016/j.coms.2014.01.001, PMID 24794262), taken at 0.90. Of head and neck squamous cell carcinomas, 15% are distantly metastatic at diagnosis, stage IVC, against 27% localized and 51% locally advanced (Barsouk A, Aluru JS, Rawla P, Saginala K, Barsouk A, 'Epidemiology, Risk Factors, and Prevention of Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma', Med Sci (Basel) 2023;11(2):42, doi:10.3390/medsci11020042, PMID 37367741). 0.90 x 0.15 = 0.135, about 9,824 patients a year
column12: a floor rather than a central estimate, and the omission that makes it one is recurrence. NCT07276399 enrols patients who are treatment-naive in the recurrent or metastatic setting, which includes the locally advanced 51% who relapse after curative treatment and have had no systemic therapy for recurrence. Published recurrence rates for that group span 22.5% to 60% across series, a four-fold range too wide to multiply by, so none of it is counted here and the eligible share is materially understated. Pushing the other way and not applied either: the study requires oropharyngeal primaries to be HPV-negative by p16, HPV DNA or high-risk HPV in situ hybridisation, excludes nasopharyngeal and unknown primaries, and requires ECOG 0 or 1

Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Head and Neck
column11: a judgement, and a tighter one than the colorectal layer carries. NCT07276399 adds amivantamab to carboplatin and pembrolizumab against the established first-line standard of pembrolizumab with platinum and 5-fluorouracil, so the layer is a share of patients already on first-line systemic therapy for recurrent or metastatic disease. The comparator is an immunotherapy backbone with no eroding share, where the colorectal comparator is an anti-EGFR agent that already reaches a minority of its own eligible population
column12: the case for lower: the study does not read out until 2029-06-18, cetuximab is the only EGFR-directed agent ever labelled in head and neck cancer and it has never displaced the platinum and pembrolizumab backbone in first line, and the HPV-negative restriction means the regimen would not be used in the growing HPV-driven oropharyngeal population. The case for higher: the primary endpoints are overall survival and response rate, and an overall survival win in first-line recurrent or metastatic head and neck cancer moves practice quickly. Settled by years of sales, not by an event

column11: already approved. RYBREVANT (openFDA drug/label set 1466c070-9f97-4fa4-a955-6a6b59981fb8, effective 2025-11-11) is indicated in locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R mutations, first line with lazertinib and after an EGFR TKI with carboplatin and pemetrexed, and in exon 20 insertion disease first line with carboplatin and pemetrexed and after platinum alone. RYBREVANT FASPRO, the subcutaneous form (set 9e58b045-e352-4f62-99bf-77fae1bebc69, effective 2026-06-17), carries the same four indications, and LAZCLUZE (set c417f9ee-2027-4ed5-92ad-3c19266de16c) the first-line one. COCOON (NCT06120140, Phase 2, 305 enrolled, primary completion 2027-05-31) enrols treatment-naive exon 19 deletion or L858R disease treated first line with amivantamab and lazertinib and randomises the dermatologic management, prophylactic antibiotics and skin care against standard care; its primary endpoint is grade 2 or worse skin adverse events at 12 weeks. PALOMA-2 (NCT05498428, Phase 2, 520 planned, primary completion 2027-08-17) gives subcutaneous amivantamab in eight cohorts, every one an EGFR-mutated NSCLC setting the label covers: first line with lazertinib (cohorts 1, 5, 6), exon 20 first line with chemotherapy (2), after osimertinib with chemotherapy with or without lazertinib (3, 3b), after amivantamab and lazertinib with chemotherapy (7), and a switch from intravenous to subcutaneous dosing (4)
column12: what the two readouts move is tolerability, dosing schedule and the subcutaneous form's share, which are reasons for more of the labelled patients to start and stay on drug. That is priced through the marketed line's growth rate, not through a layer that would sell the same patients twice. Cohort 3 adds lazertinib to the labelled post-osimertinib chemotherapy regimen; the patients are on label for the amivantamab combination today, so even a label change there adds a regimen, not a population. No pool is seeded, per the brief's rule for an approved indication
